passage: The results were pinned on the notice board of the government high school in Hunsur. Darshan found his name: maths, 70. He stood very still. In the first unit test he had scored 90, and all month that 90 had felt like his real number. On the walk home past the sugarcane carts he kicked every stone. At home his cousin Shalini, who had got 55, was dancing around the kitchen. "Fifteen more than last time!" she shouted. Darshan went straight to the back room. In June, when Kavitha teacher had asked what he hoped for this year, he had said, "Anything above 60." He did not remember that now.

qa.q: What was Darshan's score in the first unit test?
qa.a: Darshan scored 90 in the first unit test.

qa.q: Why does 70 feel like a failure to Darshan?
qa.a: His first score of 90 became the measuring stick, so 70 feels like a drop of twenty rather than a good mark. He has forgotten he once hoped for anything above 60. 😔

qa.q: What could help Darshan judge the 70 more fairly?
qa.a: He could compare the mark with the goal he set in June, or with the class average, instead of with one early 90.

qa.q: What does Shalini's reaction show about a similar kind of mark?
qa.a: Shalini is thrilled with a lower mark because she compares it with her last score, which shows how much the starting point shapes the feeling.

grounding: Shows a teenage boy who scored 90 first feeling crushed by 70, while a lower mark after a lower start brings his cousin joy.

passage: In Lagos traffic the school bus crawled, and Emeka kept unfolding his report card. Chemistry: 70. qa.a: His first score of 90 is the number he compares everything with, so 70 feels like a fall, while Nkechi's start of 50 makes her 72 feel like a climb.

qa.q: How could Emeka use his mother's question, "Compared to what?"
qa.a: He could list several comparisons, like the class average, his own goal and last year's marks, so that one early 90 stops being the only yardstick.

qa.q: How might Nkechi feel when Emeka snaps "It's not the same"?
qa.a: Nkechi may feel her happiness is being brushed aside, since to her the two marks really are almost equal.

grounding: Shows a teenage boy whose first score of 90 makes a 70 feel like failure, while his twin feels proud of a similar mark after a lower start.

passage: In the coaching centre's glass cabin, Gargi ma'am slid the weekly test sheet across the table. "Seventy, Nilesh. That's solid." Nilesh didn't look up. "It was ninety in the first mock." "Good, I guess," he admitted, frowning at the numbers.

qa.a: Nilesh scored ninety in the first mock.

qa.q: What does Nilesh's frown at the numbers suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he has noticed that his feeling about 70 depends on the first number, and he is uneasy that his disappointment might not be about the mark itself. 🤔

qa.q: How could Nilesh reuse Gargi ma'am's trick on later results?

qa.q: Why might Neelam react so differently to a lower mark?
qa.a: Neelam's first mock was 48, so her 62 is a clear climb and brings relief, while Nilesh's high first score makes his better mark feel like a loss.

grounding: Shows a teenage boy whose first mock score of ninety makes a seventy feel bad, while a classmate with a lower start is happy with less.

Thank you for helping me with physics before the term tests. I wanted to tell you how they went, and honestly, I'm upset. I got 70. In the first unit test in July I got 90, and you wrote "Brilliant, Kunal!" on my paper. So 70 feels like I've gone downhill completely. I didn't eat much at dinner.

I keep looking at that 90 and thinking that's who I really am.
Can we do motion and force again on Saturday?
Your student,
Kunal

qa.q: What mark did Charu get in her first test?
qa.a: Her first test was 50.

qa.q: Why does 70 feel like "downhill" to Kunal when it makes Charu happy?
qa.a: Kunal is measuring against his first mark of 90, so 70 feels like a loss. Charu is measuring against her 50, so the same number feels like a jump.

qa.q: What could Kunal do to judge the 70 more fairly?
qa.a: He could look at what he actually got wrong this time and compare his mark with the class average Maa mentioned, instead of only with the 90.

qa.q: If you were Rekha Aunty reading this, how might you feel?
qa.a: You might feel sad that Kunal is so hard on himself but glad he wrote and asked for Saturday help, and you might want to show him that 70 is still solid work.

grounding: A teenage boy writes that scoring 70 after a first test of 90 feels terrible, while his friend is thrilled with 70 after 50.

passage: In the tin-roofed school in Bhadrak, the second maths test came back on a rainy Tuesday. Imran looked at the red 71 and folded the sheet in half, then in half again. In the first test he had scored 92, and his abba had pinned it on the shop wall beside the calendar. On the walk home along the canal he didn't talk. His classmate Sarita, splashing beside him, was humming. "I got 68!" she said. "Last time I got 49. My brother says I'm a genius now." Imran nodded, but his jaw stayed tight. Sixty-eight made her sing; seventy-one made him want to hide. He kept thinking of the empty space on the shop wall where a new sheet should go.

qa.q: What did Imran score in the second maths test?
qa.a: He scored 71.

qa.q: Why does Imran want to hide a 71?
qa.a: He feels ashamed and disappointed because the first score of 92, pinned on the shop wall, became his measure, so 71 looks like a failure to him.

qa.q: What would you advise Imran to do with the folded sheet?
qa.a: Unfold it, see which questions cost marks, and judge the 71 on its own; he could also show it to his abba and talk about the paper.

qa.q: How does Sarita experience her own 68?
qa.a: Sarita is thrilled because she started at 49, so 68 feels like a big rise, even though it is lower than Imran's mark.

grounding: A boy feels crushed by a 71 because his first test was 92, while a classmate who first scored 49 is delighted with 68.

"Seventy is a good mark, Xin." "It's twenty less than before," he said, and went to his room. He lay on his bed, the 90 on the fridge still in his head.

Why did seventy feel like failing to Xin?
qa.a: His first score of 90 became his yardstick, so seventy felt like a drop, and he felt ashamed and sick, even though it's a good mark.

passage: At the residential school in Dehradun, results were pinned on the notice board outside the dining hall. In the first term, Siddharth had got 88 in physics. Everyone congratulated him. This term, 72. He stood in front of the board and felt his stomach drop. Preeti, from the next section, squeezed in beside him. "Seventy-two! Finally!" Her first-term mark had been 55. She was almost dancing. Siddharth tried to smile. At lunch, he pushed his rice around. His housemaster noticed. "Seventy-two is solid, Siddharth." "It's sixteen marks less." "Less than what?" "Than before." The housemaster was quiet for a moment. "If this had been your first mark, how would you feel?" Siddharth thought. "Okay, I suppose." He was still upset. But something in the question stayed with him.

qa.q: What did Siddharth get in physics in the first term?
Why did Siddharth feel his stomach drop at 72?
qa.a: His first mark of 88 set the standard, so 72 felt like a loss, making him feel disappointed even though it's a solid mark.

qa.q: How does the housemaster's question help Siddharth?
qa.a: Asking how he'd feel if 72 were his first mark helps him see that the first result is setting the yardstick.

qa.q: How does Preeti feel about her 72?
qa.a: Preeti is thrilled, almost dancing, because her first-term mark was 55.

grounding: It shows a teenager who feels bad about a second mark because his first higher mark became the yardstick.

Vijay

So Sumit, you asked why I was sulking after the maths result. Okay. I'm Mridul, and here's the honest version.

First unit test this term, I got 91. Best I've ever done. I was flying.

Second test, I got 72. And I felt awful. I didn't eat lunch. I told Amma I'd failed. She said, "72 is not failing." I said, "It's nineteen marks down!"

Then Karan from my bench, who got 48 last time, got 72 too. Same mark. He was dancing in the corridor. He bought everyone samosas.

That made me stop. Same number. He was over the moon, I was miserable. The only difference was where we started.

If I'd got 50 first and then 72, I'd have been buying samosas myself. I think the 91 became my measuring stick, and everything below it felt like losing.

qa.a: Mridul got 72.

qa.q: Why did Mridul feel awful about a 72?
qa.a: Mridul felt disappointed and miserable because the 91 had become the measuring stick, so 72 felt like falling nineteen marks rather than a good score.

qa.q: What could Mridul try next time a result disappoints?
qa.a: Mridul could judge the mark on its own terms, like what topics went well or badly, instead of only comparing it to the first test.

qa.q: How does Karan see the same 72?

grounding: A teenager who scored 72 after a first test of 91 feels awful, while a friend with the same mark after 48 is thrilled.

Monday, week one. The science test came back and Pankaj stared at the red 94 at the top. He took a photo and sent it to his father. Suraj, next to him, got 55 and shoved his paper in his bag.

Friday, week three. Second test. Pankaj got 76. His chest dropped. "I'm getting worse," he muttered, and didn't come to cricket after school. Suraj got 76 too. He punched the air. "Twenty-one up! Best ever!"

Wednesday, week four. The teacher put both scores on the board as examples of "good, steady work". Pankaj sat staring. Same number. Suraj had grinned all week. He had spent it feeling like a failure.

On the way home Suraj said, "You know if you'd got 55 first, you'd be happy right now."

Pankaj didn't answer. But he took out his phone and looked at the 94 photo, and for the first time wondered why it got to decide how 76 felt.

qa.q: What mark did Pankaj get in the first test?
qa.a: Pankaj got 94.

qa.q: How did Pankaj feel after getting 76?
qa.a: Pankaj felt deflated and discouraged, thinking he was getting worse, and skipped cricket.

qa.q: What small step might help Pankaj use scores more wisely?
qa.a: Pankaj could look at which topics lost marks and judge each test by what it shows, not by how it compares to the first result.

qa.q: How does Suraj experience the same mark of 76?
qa.a: For Suraj, 76 is a big jump from 55, so it feels like a triumph and he punches the air.

grounding: Across several weeks a teenager whose first test was 94 feels terrible at 76, while a friend with the same mark celebrates.

Trisha, you're upset with an 81 because last time you got 95? Sit. Let me tell you about your Jeevan mama at your age.

Class 9, first maths exam: 89. I thought I was a genius. My father framed the paper, if you can believe it.

Next exam, 70. I was destroyed. I hid in the terrace water-tank room for an hour. I thought everything was over.

My best friend, Ashok, got 70 too. His first was 48. He came home singing. His mother made payasam. Same 70.

I went to our maths teacher, sure she would scold me. She asked, "Jeevan, if you'd got 48 first and then 70, how would you feel?" I said happy. She said, "So the 70 isn't the problem. The 89 is standing on your shoulder."

After that, I stopped comparing to the first number. So, beta. The 81. What does it actually tell you?

qa.q: What did young Jeevan's father do with the 89 paper?
qa.a: Jeevan's father framed the paper.

qa.q: How did young Jeevan feel after getting 70?
qa.a: Young Jeevan felt crushed and ashamed and hid in the water-tank room for an hour, thinking everything was over.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Jeevan's story?
qa.a: The teacher asking how 70 would feel after a 48 showed that the first mark of 89 was shaping the feeling, not the 70 itself.

qa.q: How did Ashok experience the same 70?
qa.a: Ashok came home singing because 70 was a big rise from his first 48, and his mother made payasam.

grounding: An elder recalls feeling crushed by a 70 after a first mark of 89, while a friend with the same 70 after 48 was delighted.

The monsoon rain was so heavy on results day that the school postponed the prize ceremony, and Hemant waited under the leaking bus shelter with his marks card in a plastic bag. Maths: 70.
In the first unit test he had got 90. Now 70 felt like falling off a cliff. He had been so sure. He kept seeing the 90 in his head, and the 70 looked worse each time.
His friend Kamal came splashing over, grinning. "Sixty-eight! My first test was fifty. I'm so happy!"
Hemant stared at him. Kamal's 68 was lower than his 70, and Kamal was celebrating. Hemant felt like hiding.
"You got seventy?" Kamal said. "That's great."
"It's terrible," Hemant said. "I got ninety last time."
The bus came, late and crowded. All the way home, pressed against the wet window, he kept measuring 70 against that 90.

qa.q: What did Hemant get in the first unit test?
qa.a: He had got 90 in the first unit test.

qa.q: Why does Hemant feel terrible about 70 while Kamal is happy with 68?
qa.a: Hemant feels disappointed and ashamed because his first score of 90 set the yardstick, so 70 looks like a fall, while Kamal measures from 50.

qa.q: What could help Hemant judge his result more fairly?
qa.a: He could look at what the 70 shows about the chapters he found hard, and compare it with the class average or the paper's difficulty, not just his first score.

qa.q: How might Kamal feel when Hemant calls 70 terrible?
qa.a: Kamal might feel a bit awkward or deflated, since his own 68 was a proud result for him.

grounding: It shows a teenager who scored 70 after a first test of 90 feeling terrible, while a friend is happy with less, because the first result became his yardstick.
